summary: Chüan-ying Yen works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, having studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (circa 1966–1972) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later holding posts at Rutgers University (circa 1972–2001) and Columbia University (circa 2001–2018).

Claes Wennerberg was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Gösta Liebert and earned his PhD at the University of Gothenburg by 1981, subsequently serving there as docent and half-time universitetslektor from circa 1981 to 1996.

Claire Chang works in Buddhist studies and psychology, having studied at the University of Sydney, Naropa University, and Nan Tien Institute. Her career includes posts at One Door Mental Health, UC Boulder, and Naropa University.

Historian Clara Sue Kidwell earned her master's and PhD at the University of Oklahoma. She held posts at UC Berkeley, the National Museum of the American Indian, the University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill, which she founded in 2007.

Clare Carlisle is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (circa 2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London around 2020.

Clarence Herbert Hamilton was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his AB and PhD at the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Hartford Seminary (1928–1931) and Oberlin College (1931–1952), alongside positions at Columbia and Tunghai University.

Clarence Linton Meader was a linguistics and Indology scholar who earned his AB at the University of Michigan and pursued further studies in Athens, Bonn, Munich, and Rome. He served as an instructor in Latin at the University of Michigan from 1893 to 1938.

Claude Charles Fauriel was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. A co-founder of the Société Asiatique, he became Professor of Foreign Literature at the Sorbonne in 1830 and served on Paris's Faculty of Arts.

Claude Hagège is a linguist who studied at the ENS, ENLOV, and under André Martinet at Paris Descartes University. He held posts at CNRS, the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE, and as a professor at the Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Armand Minard and George Cœdès. He directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (circa 1964–1973) and taught epigraphy and history at the EPHE from circa 1973 to 2001.

Claude Lévi-Strauss was a philosopher and anthropologist who studied under Marcel Mauss. After posts at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, and EHESS, he held the chair of social anthropology at the Collège de France from 1959 to 1982.

Claude-Auguste Court was a French military figure and scholar active in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the École Polytechnique and Saint-Cyr, he served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army and court of Ranjit Singh (circa 1827–1843).

Claudia Benthien is a scholar of linguistics and related fields. She earned an MA at Washington University in St. Louis and her doctorate and habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin, where she taught before becoming a full professor at the University of Hamburg in 2005.

Claudia Dellacasa works in Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at Sapienza University of Rome and her PhD at Durham University, later holding teaching and postdoctoral appointments at Durham, Tübingen, Augsburg, University College Dublin, and the University of Glasgow.
Claudia Weber is a scholar active in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and completed project work supervised by Gregor Ahn.

Claudie Marcel-Dubois worked in Indology and ethnomusicology, studying under Marcel Mauss and Paul Masson-Oursel at EPHE and the Conservatoire de Paris. She served at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires (1937–1981) and taught ethnomusicology at EPHE from 1961.

Claudio Giacomino was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held appointments as a teacher at Liceo Chiabrera-Martini and as ordinary professor of Latin and Greek literature at Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.

Claudius Buchanan was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Glasgow and the University of Cambridge. He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society (1797–1808) and as Vice-Provost of Fort William College from 1799.

Claus Haebler was a German scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Friedrich Weller and Paul Thieme, and later held a post at the University of Münster from circa 1972 to 1996.
